learningObjective: Identify the purpose and effect of ATen op decomposition in PyTorch 2's compile stack.

canonicalClaims.claim: PyTorch 2's compile stack applies decomposition rules (a registered decomposition table) in AOTAutograd/pre-Inductor to rewrite composite ATen ops into simpler primitives, shrinking Inductor's op vocabulary; the table is user-extensible for custom ops.
conditions: The composite op has a registered decomposition or the user provides one.
nonImplications: Does not imply every op is fully decomposed to elementwise primitives; matmul, convolution, attention, etc. often remain opaque.
Does not imply every decomposition is faster than the composite form.

misconceptions.claim: Every ATen op is decomposed to elementwise ops before Inductor.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Matmul/conv/attention typically remain as high-level ops and go through specialized paths.
It runs pre-Inductor to normalize the graph.

misconceptions.claim: Decomposition tables are hard-coded and cannot be extended.
Decomposition is the same as functionalization.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Functionalization rewrites mutating ops into non-mutating equivalents; decomposition rewrites composites into primitives.

implementationFacts: Common decomps include layer_norm, softmax, silu, gelu
matmul/convolution/attention are typically preserved for kernel-selection paths
performanceScenarios: Decomposition shrinks Inductor's op vocabulary and allows fusion at a finer granularity; some ops are intentionally kept composite for hand-tuned kernels.
